_comment: THE INTENDED BOOT CONFIGURATION FOR BOTH NODES. The live file is /var/tmp/vllm-kv-flags/flags.json, which is per-node and NOT in git -- so this committed copy is the reviewable, recoverable source and local-ops/flags-apply.sh is what installs it. Keep them in step.
_why_not_in_flags_py_defaults: flags.py's DEFAULTS carry a deliberate invariant, stated in its own header: an EMPTY FLAGS FILE BEHAVES EXACTLY AS TODAY, every new mechanism off, so a deploy is a no-op until somebody writes a flag. Turning the disk tier on there would break that. The code defaults stay inert; this file is the configuration. The one exception is load_inflight_max, which is a SAFETY bound and belongs in the code default precisely because inert-by-default is correct for it.
_why_store_paused: THE STORE PATH STALLS THE STREAM BY ~1.1s, measured 2026-10-11 by scripts/test-meter.sh section 1 in the vllm-proxy repo: max inter-event gap 1.137s against a 0.102s baseline, A/B/A confirmed (live 1.109 / paused 0.111 / live 1.067), and located as ONE 1.052s stall 72% of the way through a 103-event stream. That suite's own header says buffering a response is a regression, not a tradeoff, so the store is PAUSED by default until the pump is bounded per step. disk_restore stays 1: reading back is the prize and costs the stream nothing. The cost of this default is that the index stops growing, so the tier serves prefixes already on disk and no new ones -- a real trade, taken deliberately in favour of every request over future restores.
